subject.title: [Feature]: Telegram — full agent activity visibility (Web UI parity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off persistent Telegram activity mode, and what disclosure, redaction, retention, and message-volume policy should it use?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but implementing it changes third-party chat disclosure and retention semantics rather than repairing a narrow broken code path.

options.title: Add guarded Telegram activity mode
options.body: Implement a default-off mode with redacted summaries, NO_REPLY/internal-turn exclusions, bounded message volume, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Keep current visibility model
options.body: Document preview/progress plus `/verbose` and `/reasoning` as the intended Telegram debug behavior and close this as not planned.

options.title: Keep detailed activity outside Telegram
options.body: Direct durable activity inspection to Control UI or another observer surface and avoid retaining detailed tool telemetry in Telegram history.

recommendation.title: Add guarded Telegram activity mode
recommendation.body: Implement a default-off mode with redacted summaries, NO_REPLY/internal-turn exclusions, bounded message volume, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses Telegram delivery, Gateway/tool-event disclosure, and security defaults, which current history and related reviews route through steipete.
